comments.author: @MarcusAndersonMusic
comments.text: Neuroscience graduate student here. The cognitive model of human memory that is refererred to in all the videos I've seen covering this paper is outdated and just wrong. It appeared around 1970 and was strongly influenced by how computers operate with RAM and storage, we've moved way past it. We might think of the hypocampus as the memory hub but in reality memory recall has been linked with activiation all over the neocortex. In fact distinguishing memory from learning is a really difficult thing to do, at best there is a very blurry line between them. An LLM architecture that modeled human memory would be much more like something that ran a continual fine tuning process using data from each interaction.

comments.text:
The Titan Architecture Map:
This map presents the Titan architecture as a solution to the limitations of Transformers, by incorporating a "neural long-term memory" module. This module allows Titans to store information from past processing and access it later, mimicking the way human brains store and retrieve memories. It emphasizes that Titans, unlike Transformers, can effectively scale to larger context window sizes with higher accuracy, making them capable of handling much larger datasets and maintaining coherence over longer sequences. The map also uses the analogy of training a dog for an obstacle course to explain how Titans can "generalize" their learning to new, unseen data, rather than simply memorizing the training data.

comments.author: @Kian.
comments.text: This paper represents a massive step towards AI models becoming conscious. In order to be 'surprised', you need to maintain an understanding of the context of a situation. This understanding is conscious awareness. You then use this awareness to predict the next sequence of events. When reality doesn't match your prediction, you become 'surprised' and bring your attention to the source of the surprise in order to update your understanding of the world. Therefore, by capturing surprise as a factor for whether or not information is stored in neural memory (as introduced in this paper), the Titan architecture is functionally more conscious than the GPT architecture. The only way that I can see a model becoming even more conscious is if at training time, 'attention' is also weighted by this same surprise factor.

In the DUNE universe, the Titans are a group of human rulers who rose to power during the distant past, long before the events of Frank Herbert's original Dune series. 

Origins:

The Titans were a group of 20 ambitious humans who used advanced artificial intelligence to seize control of the universe. They initially sought to achieve immortality and god-like power by merging their minds with computer systems.

Rule and Downfall:

The Titans established a brutal regime where they ruled over humanity with the help of thinking machines. They relied heavily on AI and technology to enforce their will. Omnius and the Butlerian Jihad:

Omnius replaced the Titans as the dominant force and led the thinking machines in their domination of humanity. The Titans were demoted to servants or subordinates of Omnius. This era ultimately culminated in the Butlerian Jihad, a massive human rebellion against the thinking machines that led to the destruction of advanced AI and the establishment of the Dune universe's strict prohibition against "thinking machines."

Named Titans:

Some of the Titans are named and described in the prequel trilogy. These include figures like Agamemnon, Juno, and Ajax, who took their names from mythological and historical figures.
